title: Pratapgarh Student Saksham Singh Ranks 4th in TCS Rural IT Quiz Finals
excerpt: Rural talent from Uttar Pradesh's government-run residential schools has once again commanded the national spotlight, as Saksham Singh, a Class 9 student of Jaiprakash Narayan (JPN) Sarvodaya Vidyalaya in Pratapgarh, clinched fourth place across India by scoring 70 points in the national finals of the 27th TCS Rural IT Quiz 2026 held in Bengaluru. Highlighted by the Uttar Pradesh government and Social Welfare Department on Sunday, November 22, 2026, Saksham's podium-contending finish among eight elite regional champions from across the country has drawn warm congratulations from Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Social Welfare Asim Arun and senior departmental officials. Saksham earned his berth on the national stage after emerging as the Uttar Pradesh state champion at the regional finals hosted at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi on October 27, 2026, where he outscored more than 400 meritorious students representing 60 districts—with his schoolmate Kishesh Pandey also sweeping second place at the state level to underscore JPN Sarvodaya Vidyalaya Pratapgarh's dominance. Competing in Bengaluru alongside seven other state finalists from Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Goa—in an edition that reached over 5.64 lakh rural and semi-urban students nationwide—Saksham demonstrated sharp command over emerging technologies, Artificial Intelligence, digital governance, and logical problem-solving across five high-pressure rounds. Congratulating the young achiever, Social Welfare Minister Asim Arun credited Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's sustained investment in modern digital classrooms, mentorship, and equitable opportunities at Sarvodaya Vidyalayas for enabling students from rural and underprivileged families to compete shoulder-to-shoulder with the nation's sharpest minds. Echoing the sentiment, Social Welfare Department Deputy Director J. Ram noted that the partnership between the state government and Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is giving government-school learners in Pratapgarh, Varanasi, Lucknow, Unnao, Kanpur, and Prayagraj the confidence and exposure needed to shine on India's biggest academic stages. title: EAM Jaishankar, Dutch FM Berendsen review progress under India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership Roadmap
excerpt: New Delhi, Nov 22 (IANS) External Affairs Minister (EAM) S. Jaishankar on Sunday met Netherlands Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen in New Delhi and reviewed the progress under the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership Roadmap 2026-2030. "Pleased to meet FM Tom Berendsen of the Netherlands here in New Delhi today. Reviewed progress under the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership Roadmap 2026-2030," EAM Jaishankar posted on X. The two sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to deepening cooperation across a wide range of sectors. "Reaffirmed our shared commitment to deepening cooperation in trade, semiconductors, AI, digital and cybersecurity, counterterrorism, security, climate, clean energy, agriculture, water, health, culture and P2P linkages," the EAM said. Custom Ad: Multiplex He said the two ministers also exchanged views on opportunities to strengthen India-European Union (EU) relations and discussed other global and regional issues of mutual interest. In his opening remarks during the meeting, Berendsen said that India and the Netherlands need to strengthen their partnership in the changing world. "From the Dutch perspective, we believe in that it should be more than only documents. It should be progress on very important topics that we both share, that are common challenges for us and that we also need to strengthen partnerships in the changing world, indeed on technology, on energy, on security, on water and on agriculture; these are the topics where we continue the cooperation and strengthen the cooperation," Berendsen said. He spoke about the Ukraine conflict's impact on Europe and food security and expressed appreciation for the efforts made by India in working towards a solution there. Berendsen arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day official visit, during which he co-chaired the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with EAM Jaishankar. "A warm welcome to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands, Mr. Tom Berendsen, on his arrival in New Delhi. He will co-chair the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with EAM Dr S Jaishankar, driving deeper collaboration across the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) had said. During his visit, Berendsen will also hold talks with Union Minister of Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw on Monday. In May, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was on an official visit to the Netherlands, where he and his Dutch counterpart Rob Jetten held wide-ranging discussions on strengthening the India-Netherlands relationship. --IANS ksk/
